column3: Contrasts believing humility and its reward with the focus's futile unbelieving deeds, under the same swift accounting.
A clear messenger's arrival does not develop the mirage, failed-deeds, or final-account movement.
Directly states the gathering, full repayment for every soul's earning, and absence of injustice.
It joins disbelief in God's signs to the identical declaration that God is swift in account.
The preceding light parable is the immediate positive counterpart to the mirage's false brightness and failed guidance.
A bounded labor-and-marriage agreement has no substantive relation to illusory deeds or reckoning.
Those who disbelieve and oppose guidance have their deeds nullified, directly clarifying the mirage's nothingness.
The immediate continuation replaces the mirage with layered darkness and declares that light comes only from God.
The disbelievers' hard Day is a broad judgment setting without the focus's false-expectation or deed imagery.
It supplies the positive counterpart: deeds of those killed in God's way will not be lost.
Rules for entering uninhabited houses do not illuminate the focus's parable or accounting.
Willing patience in Abraham's test is unrelated to deceptive appearance and final recompense.
It links each person's earned portion to God's swift account, though without the mirage of failed deeds.
Unmeasured reward for the patient is a useful positive contrast to the focus's fruitless expectation.
Noah's vindication after rejection is only a remote contrast to the focus's account of unbelieving deeds.
It exactly connects each soul's earnings, divine recompense, and God's swift account.
The nearby worship setting belongs to the light sequence that the following mirage parable reverses.
It rejects the assumption that present disbelievers are exempt from the fate of earlier deniers.
Misguiding calendar manipulation and embellished evil deeds only broadly resemble the focus's unbelief.
Instructions on modesty do not bear on the parable of apparent water and empty deeds.
Full payment for righteous works supplies the positive counterpart to deeds found empty at judgment.
God's irreversible judgment and swift accounting reinforce the focus's unavoidable reckoning.
Return to God after delayed fulfillment supports the focus's transition from apparent delay to final encounter.
Mountains becoming a mirage provide a direct image of seemingly solid reality dissolving into appearance.
The disbelievers' deeds are led astray, closely paralleling the focus's fruitless outcome.
The nearby portrait of people who fear the Day contrasts enduring worship with distracted, empty action.
It rejects reading the delay of wrongdoers' reckoning as divine neglect and fixes it to a coming Day.
False worship ends with a person's account before the true Lord and failure for disbelievers.
The same surah denies that disbelievers can escape and fixes their final destination, extending the focus's encounter with God.
Calling clear truth magic shows the false appraisal that underlies the focus's deceptive orientation.
Dhu al-Qarnayn's choice between punishment and kindness is not a mirage or accounting parallel.
The certain gathering of all people supports the focus's final encounter, though not its deeds-as-mirage image.
It denies that delayed retribution means a broken divine promise, reinforcing the certainty of the focus's account.
Unbelief causes deeds to be void, directly corresponding to the focus's seeker finding nothing.
The immediately preceding verse gives righteous people full recompense and increased bounty, the direct counterpart to 24:39.
The refusal to punish an innocent substitute concerns judicial fairness, not illusory deeds or reckoning.
The blind man's arrival does not supply a focused connection to the mirage parable.
Household-entry etiquette is unrelated to the focus's contrast between appearance and outcome.
The absence of thirst in Paradise faintly contrasts the thirsty observer of the mirage but adds no account relation.
Wealth and children as a test do not materially develop the focus's deceptive deed image.
The annihilation of mountains is a remote parallel to apparent stability being undone.
Every costly act is recorded as righteous work, giving a positive counterpart to deeds that yield nothing.
The account of watering at Midian has no relation to a mirage or divine accounting.
Universal praise and divine knowledge do not develop the focus's failed expectation or judgment scene.
Measured descent from divine stores is unrelated to the parable and its reckoning.
Truth recognized after fear is only a loose contrast to the focus's discovery after reaching its object.
Believers accept God's and the Messenger's judgment, the responsive counterpart to the focus's unbelieving trajectory.
The incapacity of false gods supports the falsity of misplaced reliance but not the focus's deed-and-account sequence.
Enduring reward with God is a broad positive counterpart without a direct mirage or accounting link.
A levelled landscape remotely echoes the dissolution of apparent solidity in the mirage image.
The sleepers' appearance differs from their reality, but the scene has no account or false-deeds dimension.
Testimony to prophethood does not illuminate the focus's parable or outcome.
The same surah states that all dominion belongs to God and that the final return is to Him.
Not expecting an account directly names the disposition that the focus overturns at its conclusion.
The description of gushing fluid does not bear on apparent water, deeds, or judgment.
The exemption concerning older women's clothing is unrelated to the focused movement.
Questioning the wonder of the cave companions is not a substantive mirage or accounting connection.
The promised real rivers and the fire's scalding water form a meaningful contrast to thirst pursuing unreal water.
The absence of unevenness in the levelled earth does not develop the focus's themes.
It explicitly asks whether disbelievers have been repaid for what they did, directly paralleling final recompense.
The legal and moral treatment of usury does not clarify the focus's false appearance or final account.
Actual rain emerging from clouds offers a limited contrast to the thirsty person's illusory water.
God's universal dominion and witness support accountability only at a very general level.
Detailed debt documentation is not a focused link to the mirage or eschatological reckoning.
The same surah depicts bodily testimony about deeds, strongly extending the accountability reached in 24:39.
Hope in God's mercy is not a substantive relation to the focus's parable.
Lying about God and denying truth lead to Hell, clarifying the fate behind the focus's unbelieving deeds.
Inherited imitation despite a call toward punishment illustrates a false course mistaken for guidance.
Wrongdoers see the Fire, know they will enter it, and find no escape, paralleling unavoidable final discovery.
It closely repeats the charge of lying about God and denying truth, with Hell as the disbelievers' abode.
The alternation of night and day as a sign does not directly develop the mirage or accounting movement.
The rushing disbelievers are not connected here to the focus's false expectation or judgment result.
Balanced spending does not illuminate the focus's image or final account.
Turning away when summoned to divine judgment is the immediate behavioral opposite of facing that judgment.
False worship is exposed as empty noise and followed by punishment for disbelief, a relevant false-practice contrast.
Purification rules do not bear on deceptive appearance or final reckoning.
People are diverted from the path while believing themselves guided, directly paralleling mirage-like false assurance.
Deniers call the arrival of a warner strange, but the verse lacks the focus's outcome and account.
Joseph's demand for an inquiry into the women's conduct is unrelated to the mirage parable.
The creation and varieties of creatures do not illuminate the focused relation.
Abraham's fulfillment of obligations does not directly address futile deeds or deceptive expectation.
Those receptive to God's signs are not deaf or blind, a clear contrast to pursuing a deceptive appearance.
The same-surah conclusion joins return to God, disclosure of what people did, and complete divine knowledge.
Good deeds not being denied provide a direct positive contrast to the null result of unbelieving works.
Prayer and purification restrictions are unrelated to the focus's mirage and accounting scene.
The chained criminals on that Day extend the punitive outcome of the focus's final reckoning.
God's knowledge of what is hidden and open only generally supports the final account.
Creation, death, and senility do not provide a focused connection.
Clear signs and divine guidance form the positive counterpart to the focus's misdirected unbeliever.
The prohibition on asserting tomorrow's action does not illuminate the focus's parable.
Individual burden-bearing and return to God clarify the personal accountability enacted in the focus.
Disbelief in God and the Messenger is tied to the prepared Blaze, reinforcing the focus's final consequence.
Concealed loyalty to those rejecting truth is a peripheral example of straying from the straight way.
It directly denies the disbelievers' assumption that they have escaped or outstripped divine power.
Divorce timing and household boundaries do not materially relate to the focused parable.
The manifest light is a direct positive counterpart to the mirage's apparent brightness and misguidance.
Concealed false assumptions about God are only a remote analogy to deceptive expectation.
Disbelief after an unmistakable sign brings exceptional punishment, reinforcing culpability after clear evidence.
A messenger as bearer of glad tidings and warning provides only a general pre-account warning context.
Fulfilling a covenant does not substantively develop the mirage, null deeds, or reckoning.
Trading guidance for error leaves the traders without profit, a concise counterpart to pursuing a promising but empty result.
Apostasy is said to nullify deeds in this world and the Hereafter, directly clarifying the focus's deeds found void.
Showy charity is compared to dust washed from a smooth rock, a close parable of apparently productive action yielding nothing.
It states the return to God followed by full payment for every soul's earnings without injustice.
It explicitly declares the works of deniers void in both worlds and denies them helpers.
Each soul finds its good and evil deeds present before it, closely supporting the focus's moment of discovery.
Every soul is fully paid at resurrection, making the focus's complete account part of the broader final recompense.
Evil is recompensed and no protector is found apart from God, reinforcing personal accountability after false security fails.
Believers describe those whose deeds became worthless after their confident claims collapsed.
Those who deny the meeting with God are described as losers when the Hour suddenly arrives.
Association with God is said to nullify even prophets' deeds, a direct boundary for the focus's nullified works.
People come to God individually and find their supposed intercessors absent, echoing the focus's collapse of expected support.
The true weighing of deeds on that Day directly develops the focus's completed account.
Those whose scales are light lose themselves because they rejected God's signs.
Denying God's signs and the meeting of the Hereafter makes deeds void and is repaid only by what was done.
The disbelievers' spending becomes a source of regret before their defeat and gathering toward Hell, exposing an effort that reverses on its agents.
The works of those associating partners are declared worthless while their punishment endures.
Earlier deniers enjoyed their share, but their works became worthless in this world and the Hereafter.
Those who do not expect the meeting with God are content with worldly life, a disposition directly opposed to the focus's final encounter.
At the gathering they recognize their loss through mutual recognition after their worldly life proves brief.
Every wrongdoer would ransom himself at judgment, showing the failure of worldly resources when recompense arrives.
Those who seek only worldly life receive its works here, establishing the misleading appearance of a complete return.
Their Hereafter portion is only Fire, and what they made and did there is rendered void.
Calling on others is compared to stretching hands toward water that will never reach the mouth, an especially close counterpart to the thirsty person's mirage.
Those who reject their Lord face the worst account and cannot ransom themselves from its outcome.
The deeds of disbelievers are compared to ashes scattered by a violent wind, a direct image of works losing all recoverable substance.
Every person's deeds are bound to him and brought out on the Day of Resurrection as an opened record.
The individual is commanded to read his own record, making the person himself sufficient witness at the account.
One who seeks only the fleeting world receives its immediate allotment but then faces Hell, a close outcome contrast to the focus.
It introduces those who are the greatest losers in their deeds, directly opening the focus's concern with failed action.
They labor in worldly life while supposing they are doing well, the clearest parallel to mistaking a mirage for water.
Their denial of God's signs and meeting makes their works worthless and leaves them without weight on the Day of Resurrection.
All faces are humbled before the Living, Sustaining One, and the wrongdoer fails at the final encounter.
Righteous work joined to faith is protected from injustice or diminution, the positive counterpart to futile deeds.
Just scales are set for the Day of Resurrection and every deed, however minute, is brought forward for accounting.
Worship based on unstable worldly benefit becomes loss in this world and the Hereafter, a close behavioral counterpart to the mirage.
Those whose scales are heavy are the successful, supplying the positive measure absent from futile deeds.
Those whose scales are light lose themselves and remain in Hell.
The deeds of disbelievers are confronted and made scattered dust, directly expressing the focus's found-nothing outcome.
Evil deeds are made alluring to deniers while they wander blindly, closely matching false appearance directing their movement.
Every soul is paid in full for what it did, and God knows their deeds completely.
Every soul is recompensed for what it earned, with no injustice and God's swift account explicitly stated.
Creation in truth culminates in every soul being recompensed for what it earned without injustice.
Those who consumed their good things in worldly life face humiliation in the Hereafter, challenging a worldly appearance of success.
Disbelief and obstruction from God's way cause deeds to go astray, directly paralleling the focus's fruitless works.
Aversion to God's revelation leads to the nullification of deeds.
God repays evildoers for what they did and rewards those who excel, framing the focus's final payment within universal recompense.
God raises people and informs them of what they did, including deeds they forgot but God preserved in full.
Receiving one's record in the right hand portrays the accountable disclosure that positively contrasts the focus's unbelieving outcome.
Receiving the record in the left hand depicts the corresponding disastrous disclosure after account.
Every person is informed of what he sent ahead and left behind, directly reinforcing complete personal reckoning.
On the overwhelming event, a person remembers what he strove for, turning past effort into present judgment.
Every soul comes to know what it sent ahead and what it left behind.
Receiving the record in the right hand begins the positive account counterpart to the focus's discovery.
That recipient receives an easy account, sharply contrasting the focus's full payment upon finding nothing.
Receiving the record from behind the back gives the corresponding adverse account scene.
Even an atom's weight of good is seen, directly affirming the exhaustive visibility of deeds.
Even an atom's weight of evil is seen, completing the focus's theme of exact recompense.
Heavy scales define a successful outcome, supplying the positive counterpart to works without weight.
Light scales lead to the abyss, a direct judgment counterpart to futile and weightless deeds.
